title: Append-only offset ledger for order-preserving log fanout and downstream replay
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: We increasingly see downstream consumers (Loki, ELK, analytics pipelines) rely on stable per-tenant ordering to correlate traces and attach large attachment blobs. Reordering and duplicate delivery during transient failures and scale events is causing incorrect correlation (broken trace->log joins) and spurious alert noise. Current ingest paths (Kafka + fronting HTTP gateway + transformer workers) have limited visibility into absolute ordering across multi-worker fanout and make replay idempotency brittle.

Proposal: Implement an append-only offset ledger service that maintains a single monotonic offset per tenant+source shard for every ingested log batch. Producers write batches with a proposed offset range and an idempotency key; the ledger atomically commits the offset range or rejects it if overlapping. The ledger will be the source of truth for ordering and enable downstream ordered fanout, deterministic replay APIs, and compacted snapshot reconciliation for worker restarts. Ledger storage will be implemented on CockroachDB (or Dynamo where applicable) with nightly compaction and TTL for cold tenants. The ledger is intentionally append-only to simplify reasoning, make replays deterministic, and allow compact checkpoints for large-tenancy customers.

Why different from other ingest work: Unlike schema-enforcers or enrichment shims, this ticket focuses on a global ordering primitive and replay surface that other subsystems can build on (transformers, enrichers, Loki adapters). It should reduce duplicate-delivery work and provide a simpler migration path to multi-region ordering policies.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger service exposes HTTP/gRPC write and read APIs supporting proposed offset ranges and idempotency keys
Producers can obtain a committed offset per-batch; downstream fanout uses committed offsets to emit events in strict offset order
Replays via ledger range API can be consumed by transformer workers to reconstruct exact ingestion sequences with <=1s cold-start sketch times
Integration test harness demonstrates zero ordering violations for 99.99% of synthetic multi-worker writes under network partitions and worker restarts
Metric set (ordering_violations, replay_lag_ms, commit_rate, rejected_overlaps) emitted to Grafana and dashboard created
Migration plan documented: incremental switch for one tenant, test tenant-level compaction, rollback steps
plan: Week 1: Design ledger schema and API, choose primary storage (CockroachDB prototype); draft conformance tests
Week 2: Implement basic ledger commit/read endpoints + idempotency handling; unit tests
Week 3: Wire writer into ingest-proxy as opt-in path; add integration test harness simulating multi-worker fanout
Week 4: Implement replay endpoint + snapshot checkpointing and compaction; run chaos tests (partition, restarts)
Week 5: Create migration runbook, instrument dashboards, start gradual rollout to non-critical tenants
Week 6: Expand to high-traffic tenants, monitor metrics, finalize docs and handoff
risks: Leader contention: single-shard commit hot spots under bursty tenants; mitigated by sharding by tenant-source and optimistic batching
Storage cost for high-cardinality tenants if offsets are retained for too long; mitigated by TTL/compaction and cold-tier snapshots to S3
Producer adoption complexity: changing producer contract to provide idempotency keys and handle rejections requires coordination with transformer teams
Operational complexity: need observability for ledger health (stuck commits, high retry rates) and runbook for DB failover
testing: Unit tests for ledger atomic commit and idempotency semantics
Integration test with synthetic producer cluster (10 workers) asserting monotonic offsets and no duplicates
Chaos test scenarios: network partition between writers and ledger, DB transient errors, leader failover
Performance test: sustained 20k commits/sec aggregated with latency SLO target <50ms p95
Migration smoke tests: roll-forward and rollback on a staging tenant
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal team only (opt-in per-tenant) for 48h
Beta: non-critical customers (2 tenants) with double-write (ledger + legacy) to compare outputs
Gamma: gradual ramp for small production tenants with monitoring guardrails and automatic rollback on ordering_violations spike
GA: open for all tenants after 2 weeks stable and proven reduction in reorder incidents
comments: 2026-02-10 Sofia Patel: Created ticket after post-mortem describing two customer incidents where trace->log correlation failed due to replay reordering. Proposed append-only ledger to give deterministic ordering surface.

2026-02-11 Ethan Chen: Spike results: Cockroach prototype can sustain ~12k commits/s per 3-node cluster with p95 commit latency ~37ms; will need sharding strategy for high-cardinality tenants. Uploaded perf numbers to Confluence.

2026-02-12 Priya Rao (transformers): Raised integration concern: transformers expect best-effort offset and cannot block on ledger writes today. Plan: expose opt-in producer mode and a fast-fail path where legacy behavior is preserved.
2026-02-14 DevOps note (Aarav Singh): DB availability plan drafted. We should provision a read-replica pool for replay consumers and add circuit-breaker thresholds for commit latencies.
